items.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Patato’s there [Carlos Valdez]. Don Alias is there. ... I never did any more with him.

ctx.x: Yeah, apoplectic. He was like [Liebman inhales deeply]. He was like this – at one point, four or five hours into the session, he’s like, “I can’t take it. My sessions are like laboratories. They don’t even bring their wives.” He was like that. I said, “Manfred, it’s New York City. This is drummers. It’s New York City.” Patato’s there [Carlos Valdez]. Don Alias is there. You’re talking about guys like joie de vivre, for Christ’s sake, and it’s New York City. This is drum land. And the guy’s like this. I thought…
Around that time, as you mentioned, in the late ’70s, early ’80s, you decided to put the tenor aside . . .
